text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] serving-cluster-prod: elevated 5xx rate + RDMA link flaps detected across rack-east-3, auto-page sent to oncall
kevin (oncall): I'm on it. seeing ~30% 5xx on /v1/generate and many containers restarting with CUDA OOM around the same time.
maria (eng-runtime): getting kernel logs from node gpu-23: 'mlx5_core 0000:86:00.0: IB device 'mlx5_0' pkey violation / port state DOWN' and repeated retransmit counters.
anjali (sre): packetloss on IB fabric, full port flaps. ibstat shows port 1 down intermittently. flow control causing RPC retries -> queue growth -> local GPU OOMs.
sam (infra): rolling probe shows a subset of top-of-rack switches showing increased qloss on IB paths to rack-east-3. Not correlated to power or fabric config changes.
nicole (cust-sre): flagged two paying customers seeing degraded latency and 502s. they're being notified with a brief incident note.
kevin (oncall): quick mitigation plan: 1) move serving traffic off rack-east-3 -> route to rack-west-1, 2) reduce batch_size + throttle ingress to reduce memory pressure, 3) if IB flaps persist enable TCP fallback for inter-node RPCs. executing step 1 now.
maria (eng-runtime): thumbs up. lowering default batch_size to 4 for running replicas and enabling per-route token cap. patch pushed to rollout channel.
opsbot: deploying runtime-config patch v2026.3.4 to serving-deployment (canary 10%)
kevin (oncall): starting weighted traffic shift off rack-east-3 (20% -> 60% over 5m). watching error rate.
15m later
maria (eng-runtime): error rate dropped from 32% to 9% after traffic shift + batch change. still seeing container restarts on nodes that lost IB connectivity. logs show repeated `cudaErrorUnknown: allocating 0x...` before process exit.
anjali (sre): decided to cordon affected nodes and drain replicas. running `kubectl drain gpu-23 gpu-24 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then letting autoscaler recreate elsewhere.
sam (infra): while draining, I see mlx5 driver reporting firmware ISR timeout on those NICs. planning a controlled restart of RDMA stack: `modprobe -r mlx5_core mlx5_ib; modprobe mlx5_core mlx5_ib` then restart the daemons. hitting them one at a time.
kevin (oncall): be careful — restarting RDMA drivers will disrupt any remaining jobs on node. confirm drain completed first.
opsbot: drain completed on gpu-23, gpu-24. moving to driver restart.
sam (infra): restarted RDMA stack on gpu-23 successfully. IB port came back up, but counters show persistent CRC errors on that link. scheduled to leave it isolated until full swap.
maria (eng-runtime): for immediate stability I've enabled RPC TCP fallback for serving-rpc on the control plane: `REDWOOD_RPC_TRANSPORT=prefer_rdma,allow_tcp` -> `prefer_tcp_if_errors`. will monitor for perf regression.
kevin (oncall): after TCP fallback, container restarts dropped to near zero and 5xxs are ~2%. latency increased by ~12% p95 on some ops but acceptable for now.
nicole (cust-sre): sent updates to impacted customers: short explanation, mitigation steps, ETA for full fabric fix. customers acknowledged.
pagerduty-bot: paging note: handoff scheduled at 08:00 UTC to oncall next shift @anjali.
kevin (oncall): prepping handoff: summary -> RDMA link degradation in rack-east-3 caused retransmits and RPC retries, which allowed request queues to grow and triggered CUDA OOMs on some serving containers. Mitigations executed: traffic shift, reduced batch_size, node drains, RDMA driver restarts, enabled TCP fallback. Current status: traffic normalized, degraded links isolated, monitoring in place.
anjali (sre): taking over. next steps I'm tracking: 1) coordinate with networking to replace affected NICs/links, 2) run longer IB stress tests overnight (`ib_send_bw -F` + error monitoring), 3) root cause investigation on why CRC errors started (firmware? cabling?).
maria (eng-runtime): also scheduled runtime change: automatic TCP-fallback policy if retransmit rate > 0.5% for 3m. will open RFC for permanent fallback thresholds.
sam (infra): I've opened a hw ticket with the switch vendor and asked datacenter to inspect cabling for rack-east-3.
nicole (cust-sre): will keep customers informed and coordinate a status page update if we extend mitigation.
kevin (oncall): tagging this as page->resolved for now, leaving the incident open for followup and postmortem. recommend blameless postmortem, include workload evals to avoid queue growth on retries.
incident-bot: Incident status changed -> MONITORING. Attachments: runbook link <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/ib-flap>| runbook, incident playbook.
anjali (sre): agreed. I'll consolidate logs and hand off to runtime + infra for root cause. assigning action items in the incident board.
maria (eng-runtime): quick debug note to include in postmortem: saw a tight correlation between RPC retry storms and batch_size/kvcache growth which amplified memory usage. include tuned cache eviction and early-shed heuristics in remediation.
kevin (oncall): thanks all. handing to @anjali. I'll be available for followups. :thumbsup:
